main_text.l: Sunt Enunciata simplicia vel composita. Nam de
individuo seu specie seu substantia enuntiantur seu
prædicantur, aut Genus, aut Differentia, aut Proprium,
aut Accidens, aut quantitas, aut qualitas, aut relatio,
aut actio, aut passio, aut quando, aut ubi, aut situs,
aut habitus, quæ omnia Enunciata efficiunt.
Hactenus de Enunciatis dictum est.

tur Quæstio, ad cujus fidem tertio argumento opus

Argumentum autem dicitur tertium (vulgò
me-dius terminus) quia in qualibet Quæstione seu enun-

probatio ex aliquo Inventionis loco deprompta,
tertium argumentum constituit.

page.notes: Running head is "DE DIALECTICA." with a period-like mark after it; transcribed without the mark. The first line is a fragment continuing from the previous page. "Lucæ16." is printed with no visible space. Long s has been normalised to s throughout. The ornamental rule below the paragraph about Enunciata is not text and is not transcribed. Faint show-through of text from the reverse side appears at the right margin and in the lower half; it is not transcribed. Dark staining at the top right corner. The heading "Quid est Syllogismus?" has an underlined initial Q. "Quæstio" in the running text is underlined. The word "Syllogismus" in the first paragraph has a drop-cap S; the S is joined to the following letters. "ein schlußrede" is in black letter and marked accordingly.
